title: TypeScript SDK: refresh tool calling + structured output examples; tighten types; streaming sample runs
creator: Monica Patel
description:
Goal
Refresh TypeScript SDK developer-facing examples and types so that:
- tool calling examples match the canonical semantics (tool definitions, arguments validation, parallel tool calls, tool-result messages)
- structured output examples demonstrate JSON schema constraints + robust validation
- streaming examples compile and run end-to-end, with consistent event handling and final message assembly

Context
We have cross-language inconsistency in streaming/tool calling snippets and recurring support issues:
- partial tool-call args mid-stream causing premature JSON.parse failures
- mismatch between docs payload shape and TS types leading to type errors and confusion
- streaming samples that "look" right but don’t compile/run as copy/paste due to outdated imports or event unions

Scope (TypeScript)
1) Tool calling types + example parity
- Tighten tool call/event typing so the example code can be both correct and readable.
- Ensure the example demonstrates parallel tool calls (where the model returns >1 tool call) and tool-result messages.
- Document the "accumulate then parse" rule for tool call arguments during streaming.

2) Structured output example (JSON schema)
- Add a schema-constrained output example that validates the final JSON using a runtime validator.
- Include fallback guidance for invalid JSON: retry with a stricter system message and/or switch to non-streaming for the structured call.

3) Streaming example refactor
- Adopt the canonical streaming event model conventions used across SDKs.
- Ensure the streaming sample compiles with current SDK version and runs via package scripts.
- Add minimal but explicit error branches (disconnects, unexpected event shapes).

Non-goals
- Any breaking change to the API protocol.
- New product features for structured output/tool calling.

Implementation notes / decisions
- Event handling: examples should treat streaming as an event log. Do not assume tool-call arguments arrive in a single chunk.
- Tool args parsing: accumulate toolCall.argumentsText deltas into a buffer and only JSON.parse once the tool call is marked complete.
- Validation: examples should use a lightweight runtime validation approach (e.g., zod) to demonstrate safe parsing and good errors. Keep the schema small and realistic.
- Parallel tool calls: show the loop that executes multiple tool calls and returns tool results back to the model in the correct message shape.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Tool calling example compiles and runs; demonstrates tool definitions, execution, and tool-result messages
- [x] Types are tightened enough to prevent the common mismatch (tool result shape / union narrowing) but not so heavy that examples become unreadable
- [x] Structured output example demonstrates JSON schema and runtime validation; includes retry guidance
- [x] Streaming example compiles and runs; handles deltas + final assembly consistently
- [x] Examples align with canonical naming/terminology approved by PM
- [x] PRs include a short migration note if a previously documented shape is being corrected

Links / artifacts
- Canonical conventions: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/streaming-event-model-conventions.json
- Tool calling parity guidelines: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/sdk-guides/tool-calling-parity-guidelines.json
- Structured output guidance: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/sdk-guides/structured-output-json-schema-guidance.json
- Support pain points: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues/top-support-issues-streaming-and-tools.json
updates: 2025-02-05 (Dana Lo): Started with audit of current TS examples vs Python/Go. Main mismatch is tool result typing and streaming tool-call args: our snippet JSON.parse()’d inside the event loop, which fails on partial args. Drafted plan: introduce an accumulator helper in the example (not SDK API) and tighten the union types for events so narrowing is straightforward.

2025-02-07 (Dana Lo): Met with Ibrahim Khan + Brian Murphy to confirm example-level payload shape. Agreement: examples should show (1) content deltas, (2) tool_call delta events with partial args, (3) a final event to indicate completion, then the code assembles the final assistant message and executes tools. Added a reviewer note: avoid implying that tool args are always valid JSON mid-stream.

2025-02-10 (Dana Lo): Opened PR #1932 to update tool calling types + examples. Key change: tool call event types now model arguments as text deltas and provide a stable place for toolCallId/name. Example updated to support multiple tool calls returned in a single assistant turn. Added explicit tool-result message shape to feed results back.

2025-02-12 (Wei Chen): Docs parity review on #1932. Request: ensure terminology matches docs ("tool calling" + "tool results"), and add a comment that parallel tool calls are model-driven (not guaranteed). Also requested we keep the example minimal and link to runnable sample in redwood-examples once merged.

2025-02-14 (Dana Lo): Addressed review: improved naming in snippet, added small helper function assembleToolArgs(toolCallId) that buffers deltas and only parses when complete. Added try/catch around parse with a helpful error message pointing users to the "Known pitfalls" doc section.

2025-02-17 (Dana Lo): Opened PR #1940 to refactor streaming sample event handling. Adjusted imports and updated sample to compile with current SDK. Added minimal logging of event types and a final assembly step so users can see the full assistant message. Included error handling for stream abort/disconnect (example suggests retry with idempotency key where supported).

2025-02-19 (Dana Lo): Support feedback: Dev Patel flagged SUP-18452 as the canonical issue—type mismatch in older snippet. Added a migration note in the TS README section: previous snippet treated tool results as an untyped object; new snippet uses a discriminated union and the exact tool_result message shape.

2025-02-21 (Dana Lo): Opened PR #1951 for structured output example using JSON schema + runtime validation (zod). Example demonstrates a small schema (array of steps with constrained enums) and shows: (a) validate, (b) surface validation errors, (c) retry guidance (stricter prompt / non-stream call). Added note: don’t attempt incremental JSON parsing while streaming; validate only final assembled content.

2025-02-25 (Nikhil Sharma): PM sign-off on public terminology used in TS examples ("structured output"; avoid "JSON mode" unless in compatibility section). Requested we include a one-line callout that model support varies and to consult the support matrix page. No further changes required.

2025-02-27 (Dana Lo): All three PRs approved and merged. Verified locally: pnpm install && pnpm -C examples ts-node streaming.ts and tool-calling.ts run successfully. Structured output example passes validation path and demonstrates retry on intentionally invalid output. Coordinated with Connor O'Brien for release versioning and changelog blurb.

2025-03-04 (Connor O'Brien): Released redwood-sdk-typescript-2.9.0 with refreshed examples. Post-release check: docs code tabs render correct TS snippet (after docs PRs). Monitoring support trend for tool-call type mismatch and JSON parse errors over next 2 weeks.
comments: Brian Murphy (2025-02-07): Please make sure the example does not imply that tool args are delivered as JSON per chunk. We should explicitly buffer deltas and parse once the tool call is complete to avoid repeating SUP-18421 in TS land.

Ibrahim Khan (2025-02-08): Keep the example’s tool execution deterministic for golden transcripts. If you include parallel tool calls, ensure the example orders execution by tool_call_id to avoid flaky output in docs/tests.
Wei Chen (2025-02-12): For structured output, we should recommend runtime validation even when schema-constrained output is enabled. Users assume it’s always perfect; we need a safe pattern.
Dev Patel (2025-02-19): +1 to adding a migration note. The top confusion is copying the snippet and then fighting TS type errors; make the example compile with strict settings out of the box.
resolution: Merged PRs #1932 (tool calling types + examples), #1940 (streaming event handling refactor), and #1951 (structured output JSON schema + validation example). Released in redwood-sdk-typescript-2.9.0. Examples now buffer tool-call arg deltas before parsing, support parallel tool calls, and validate structured output with runtime schema checks.
